title: optimize: NCCL collectives + KVCache overlap scheduling and continuous batching for tensor-parallel
author: Samir Rao
description: Motivation: Reduce multi-GPU tail latency and improve throughput for tensor-parallel workloads by better overlapping NCCL collectives, kernel execution, and KV cache lookups under continuous batching. Changes in this PR combine scheduler heuristics, lightweight kernel-level sync points, and NCCL stream/priority tuning to increase compute/comm overlap and reduce idle GPU time. Scope: - Add scheduling policy that prioritizes collectives on a dedicated high-priority NCCL stream when kernel work can proceed on default streams. - Introduce lightweight kernel sync markers to avoid unnecessary stream synchronization when KV cache hits are pending. - Enable async NCCL collective paths when safe for model sharding patterns and fall back on sync for edge-cases. - Tune stream priorities and CUDA stream ordering for common 8/16-GPU TP configs. - Improve continuous batching hot-path to keep KV cache warm and reduce memcpy stalls. Checklist: - [x] Scheduler heuristic implemented and unit-tested - [x] NCCL stream priority toggle behind runtime flag - [x] KV cache sync points added with opt-out - [x] End-to-end perf harness added for 8/16 GPU cluster tests - [x] Documentation + release note drafted Related work: ENG-7230, ENG-7123. Risk: Changes gated behind runtime feature-flag `tp_nccl_overlap_v2` and default to previous behavior. This is focused on runtime only; model correctness unchanged.

review_comments: Olivia Park: Nice work, this addresses the p99 tail we saw in production. A few questions: why do we prefer a dedicated high-priority stream vs priority ordering on the default stream?

Samir Rao: Dedicated stream gives us explicit overlap without forcing kernels to run on non-default streams; it avoids changing kernel submission paths and is less invasive for existing sync assumptions.
Diego Alvarez: Can we add a fatal assertion when user enables async collectives on unsupported topology? We saw a correctness risk on 4-node mixed NVLink configs.
Samir Rao: Added topology guard in stream_manager.cc and falls back to sync collectives when detected; updated tests to cover the mixed-NVLink case.
Evelyn Zhang: Tests look good; please add an opt-out env var for debugging and document it in the rollout guide.
Samir Rao: Added TP_NCCL_OVERLAP_DEBUG env var and documented it.
notes: Performance: In our perf lab runs with 8xA100 80GB the change improved throughput by ~9% at batch size 16 and reduced p99 latency by ~12% for typical seq_len=1024 generative workloads.
Safety: Feature gated behind tp_nccl_overlap_v2 and controlled rollout recommended (canary on dedicated capacity).
Operational: Added metrics runtime.nccl.overlap_enabled and runtime.kvcache.async_hits to console dashboards.
release_notes: Improve multi-GPU tensor-parallel throughput and p99 by better overlapping NCCL collectives with kernel execution and KV cache access; feature gated behind tp_nccl_overlap_v2. Rollout: gradual canary recommended.
